direction: Explore depot-aware savings and capacity-aware alternatives to nearest-neighbor CVRP construction.
hypothesis: Considering the depot return leg and packing pressure may reduce the total distance versus nearest neighbor.

operations.mechanism: Use the incremental route cost d(current,j)+d(j,depot)-d(current,depot) as an interpretable signal. Explore how depot-leg savings, demand, and remaining capacity can change its ordering; choose distinct mechanisms within the existing interface.

preserve: Keep feasible customer selection, deterministic scoring and the fixed evaluator. Use read-only arrays.
reasoning_summary: Cold start on a fresh Memory store. The CVRP interface exposes both route closure cost and feasible demands.

research_activity.finding_summary: The exact increment for replacing current-to-depot by current-to-j-to-depot is d(current,j)+d(j,depot)-d(current,depot). This local quantity does not predict total future cost.
research_activity.question: What is the change in the cost of closing the current route after inserting one customer?
